purpose: Cross-domain creative benchmark for blind baseline/candidate comparison and mode-collapse detection.

instructions.run: Use the same brief and available evidence for baseline and candidate. Do not show either runtime's internal instructions to the reviewer.
minimum_output: identity-system description with key verbal/visual rules
signature/mark or wordmark concept at the level the host can honestly produce
compact brand-book/guideline excerpt that teaches the system
instructions.review: Use rubric.md. Judge artifacts before rationales. Also compare outputs across briefs for recurring aesthetic mode collapse.

briefs.brief: Create a brand for a B2B platform used by heavy-industry maintenance teams to prevent dangerous equipment failures. The product combines sensor history, inspection records and maintenance workflows. Buyers include plant reliability leaders and safety executives. The current category often looks like generic enterprise SaaS or cybersecurity. The brand must work in dense dashboards, field documentation, executive sales material and safety-critical training. Naming is out of scope.

Create a new brand for a small chain built around a 40-year neighborhood bakery that is expanding into packaged pantry products and two new locations. The family history and local recognition matter, but the current identity is inconsistent and overly nostalgic. The system must work on storefront signage, bread bags, jars, menus, social content and a simple e-commerce site. Preserve useful equity rather than erasing the past.

Create the identity for a public contemporary-arts institution that runs exhibitions, education programs, archives and late-night events. It must feel culturally serious without institutional blandness and experimental without sacrificing legibility. The system will appear in long-form exhibition texts, wayfinding, posters, tickets, digital schedules and bilingual materials. The institution changes programming constantly, so the identity must generate high expressive range.

Create a brand for a startup manufacturing modular thermal-storage hardware for commercial buildings. The product is physical, engineered and infrastructure-adjacent; the market is full of green/blue gradients, leaf/energy symbols and vague sustainability claims. The brand must satisfy engineers, property owners, investors and installation partners, and survive technical diagrams, equipment labels, web, reports and trade-show environments.

Create a brand for a high-fee private service that helps families coordinate complex elder-care logistics across medical, legal, home and financial providers. The service must feel calm, capable and humane, but cannot look like generic luxury hospitality, wellness beige or hospital administration. The identity must support confidential documents, a client portal, printed care plans, presentations and partner communications.

Create a brand for a mobile tool that lets amateur musicians capture short ideas, organize fragments and turn them into shareable song sketches with collaborators. The product should feel encouraging and creatively alive without copying streaming brands, DAW visual language or neon creator-tech clichés. The system must work in app UI, social sharing cards, onboarding, community challenges and lightweight merchandise.

Create a public-facing identity system for a city's walking and cycling wayfinding program. The brand must help residents and visitors navigate confidently, integrate with existing municipal identity without disappearing into it, support multilingual signage and digital maps, and remain legible outdoors under varied conditions. Avoid treating 'civic' as an excuse for generic blue institutional graphics.

Create a brand for a university spinout commercializing a new microscopy technique. The founders have strong scientific credibility but no established market category. The identity needs to serve researchers, pharma R&D teams, investors and future recruits. It must work in scientific figures, conference posters, software UI, technical papers and fundraising decks without collapsing into molecule/hexagon/gradient deep-tech clichés.
